Duplicity

/doo-PLIS-ih-tee/ - the stress falls on PLIS · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Duplicity means deliberate, two-faced deceitfulness.

The novel's charm curdles once readers spot the narrator's duplicity: he mourns his brother in the public chapters and toasts his ruin in the private letters.

Worked Example

For two seasons, the assistant coach praised the starting goalkeeper in team meetings while quietly urging recruiters from a rival club to poach her. When one recruiter's email surfaced, the players did not call it a mistake; they called it duplicity, because both faces had been worn on purpose, for months.

Duplicity is more specific than lying or deceit: it means running two faces at once - keeping one story alive for one audience and its opposite for another, deliberately and over time. One lie is deceit; a double life is duplicity.

How Duplicity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

deceit

deceit: any dishonesty, even a single lie

double-dealing

double-dealing: working both sides of a bargain for yourself

treachery

treachery: betrayal of a trust - the hidden knife actually falling

Antonyms

honesty

honesty: plain truthfulness

sincerity

sincerity: meaning what you say and show

How Strong Is It? — dishonesty → duplicity → treachery

dishonesty vs. duplicity

dishonesty vs. duplicity: Dishonesty covers any straying from the truth, down to a fib about homework; duplicity is a heavier charge - a sustained double game.

treachery vs. duplicity

treachery vs. duplicity: Treachery goes past duplicity: the duplicitous keep two faces in play, while treachery is the moment the hidden face strikes and the trust is actually betrayed.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of duplicity.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — du-

Prefix — du-: two

Root — plic-

Root — plic-: to fold (Latin plicare)

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: state of being

Put it together

Put it together: Du- (two) + plic- (Latin plicare, 'to fold') + -ity (the state of being) = the state of being folded double. A duplicitous person is literally two-fold: one self folded behind another. The folding root is everywhere in English - duplicate, complicated (folded together), and duplex, a building folded into two homes.

Use the root in a new word: duplex

Use the root in a new word: duplex: Their duplex is literally a two-fold house: one building folded into two front doors and two separate homes.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Duplicity is a formal accusation of sustained two-facedness; for a single lie, deceit or dishonesty is enough. Its cousin hypocrisy, which you met in Unit 1, blames people for violating values they preach; duplicity blames them for deliberately running two contradictory stories at once.
